grammar.title: Inversion After Negative Adverbials
grammar.explanation:
When a negative or restrictive adverbial opens a clause, English flips the subject and the auxiliary verb. **"Never have I seen"** replaces the flat "I have never seen," and the sentence gains instant emphasis.

This **inversion** belongs to formal registers: speeches, essays, and serious journalism. It turns a plain denial into a rhetorical event, which is why politicians and editorial writers love it.

The pattern works after **"never," "rarely," "seldom," "hardly," "scarcely," "barely," "not only," "no sooner,"** and **"only"** phrases such as **"only then"** or **"only by."** Choose the auxiliary that fits the tense: **do/does/did, have/has/had, will/would, can/could.**

Mind the pairings that follow the inversion. **"No sooner"** pairs with **"than,"** while **"hardly"** and **"scarcely"** pair with **"when."** Mixing them up, for example **"no sooner ... when,"** is the classic C2-level slip.
examples: *Never before have* residents embraced **tactical urbanism** so quickly. (formal emphasis with present perfect)
*Not only did* the council approve **pedestrianization**, it funded new parks as well. (not only + did)
*Hardly had* the market opened *when* the old **food desert** was forgotten. (hardly pairs with when)
*Seldom has* **placemaking** transformed a neighborhood so completely. (seldom + has)
*Only by* listening to locals *can* true **urbanism** succeed. (only by + can)
*Rarely do* visitors notice the clever **wayfinding** at first glance. (rarely + do)

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: "I have never seen such clever wayfinding."
practice.a: Never have I seen such clever wayfinding.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: "The council not only approved pedestrianization; it funded new parks."
practice.a: Not only did the council approve pedestrianization; it funded new parks.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: "The market had hardly opened when the crowds arrived."
practice.a: Hardly had the market opened when the crowds arrived.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: "Residents seldom embrace tactical urbanism so quickly."
practice.a: Seldom do residents embrace tactical urbanism so quickly.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: "True urbanism can succeed only by listening to locals."
practice.a: Only by listening to locals can true urbanism succeed.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: "The fees had no sooner started than traffic fell."
practice.a: No sooner had the fees started than traffic fell.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: "I rarely read hyperlocal news, but this story caught my eye."
practice.a: Rarely do I read hyperlocal news, but this story caught my eye.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: "She had barely finished the placemaking plan when the mayor called."
practice.a: Barely had she finished the placemaking plan when the mayor called.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: "A third place has seldom mattered so much to a neighborhood."
practice.a: Seldom has a third place mattered so much to a neighborhood.

practice.q: Rewrite with inversion: "You will understand the fifteen-minute city only then."
practice.a: Only then will you understand the fifteen-minute city.
